'''Peter Kramer''' (16 March 1933 – 23 April 2026) was a German physicist.

== Background ==
Kramer studied physics at the [[University of Münster]], the [[University of Tübingen]], the [[University of Bristol]] and the [[University of Marburg]].  He received his PhD in 1964 in Marburg and in 1968 his Habilitation
in Tübingen. He was a postdoc at the [[UNAM]] in [[Mexico City]], where he collaborated with [[Marcos Moshinsky]].
He was a professor at the Institute for Theoretical Physics in Tübingen from 1970 until 1998 when he retired. He has also served as a Dean and a Vice President at the University of Tübingen.  Kramer married in 1962 and has two children.

Kramer died on 23 April 2026, at the age of 93.<ref>[https://www.trauer.swp.de/traueranzeige/peter-kramer Peter Kramer]</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Kramer's work is concerned with applications of [[Group Theory|groups]] and [[Representation Theory|representations]] in [[mathematical physics]]. His early work was in [[nuclear physics]]. In the early eighties he and his student Roberto Neri developed a mathematical model for [[Quasi-crystal|quasiperiodic tesselations]] of three-dimensional space.  Their paper was submitted in 1983 and published in 1984,<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1107/S0108767384001203|title=On periodic and non-periodic space fillings of E<sup>m</sup> obtained by projection|year=1984|last1=Kramer|first1=P.|last2=Neri|first2=R.|journal=Acta Crystallographica A |volume=40|page=580|issue=5|bibcode=1984AcCrA..40..580K }}</ref> a few months before [[Dan Shechtman]] and his co-workers announced the experimental discovery of an [[alloy]] with [[icosahedral]] quasi-crystalline structure.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1951|title=Metallic Phase with Long-Range Orientational Order and No Translational Symmetry|year=1984|last1=Shechtman|first1=D.|last2=Blech|first2=I.|last3=Gratias|first3=D.|last4=Cahn|first4=J.|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=53|page=1951|bibcode=1984PhRvL..53.1951S|issue=20|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Icosahedral Crystals in Perspective|year=1990|last1=Nelson|first1=D.R.|journal=Science|volume=249|issue=4965|page=111|bibcode=1990Sci...249..111N|doi=10.1126/science.249.4965.111-b|s2cid=98427731 }}</ref> Shechtman was awarded the 2011 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] for his work.

In later years, Kramer became interested in [[cosmology]] and three-dimensional [[space form]]s. His scientific œuvre contains more than 200 publications.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://homepages.uni-tuebingen.de/peter.kramer/ |title = Symmetry in Physics}}</ref>

== Publications ==
* P. Kramer, G. John and D. Schenzle: ''Group Theory and the Interaction of Composite Nucleon Systems.'' Vieweg, Braunschweig 1981
* P. Kramer and M. Saraceno: ''Geometry of the Time-dependent Variational Principle in Quantum Mechanics.'' Lecture Notes in Physics 140, Springer, Berlin 1981
* P. Kramer and R. Neri: ''On periodic and non-periodic space fillings of E<sup>m</sup> obtained by projection.'' In: ''Acta Crystallogr.'' A '''40''', 1984, 580-587 {{doi|10.1107/S0108767384001203}}
* P. Kramer and A. Mackay: ''Crystallography: Some answers but more questions.'' In: ''Nature'' '''316''', 1985, 17-18 {{doi|10.1038/316017a0}}
* P. Kramer: ''Gateways towards quasicrystals.'' 2010 [https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0061v1 arXiv:1101.0061v1]
* P. Kramer: ''Platonic topology and CMB fluctuations: homotopy, anisotropy and multipole selection rules.'' In: ''Class. Quantum Grav.'' '''27''', 2010, {{doi|10.1088/0264-9381/27/9/095013}}
